text: Real merit of any kind, 'ubi est non potest diu celari'; it will be discovered, and nothing can depreciate it but a man's exhibiting it himself. It may not always be rewarded as it ought, but it will always be known.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CXI, to his son, London, April 30, Old Style 1750
